summary: Defines MIB objects, in SMIv2 format, for managing IEEE 802.5 Token Ring subnetworks with SNMP. It is a draft standard and updates the earlier RFC 1743.

eli5.summary: A set of gauges for checking on a ring-shaped network where a token is passed around.

questions: how to manage token ring with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP management objects for checking on and controlling IEEE 802.5 Token Ring interfaces.

tldr.problem: Network managers using SNMP needed a standard set of objects for the state, settings and error counts of IEEE 802.5 Token Ring interfaces, written in the newer SNMPv2 format.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a MIB module named dot5 with an Interface Table, a Statistics Table, an obsolete Timer Table, test identifiers and chip-set identifiers, plus compliance rules.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 1231 and RFC 1743 and is a Draft Standard that has since been updated by RFC 1749.

today: RFC 1748 is a Draft Standard that replaced RFC 1231 and RFC 1743, and it has been updated by RFC 1749.

sections.title: What This MIB Is For
sections.content:
RFC 1748 defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) used by network management protocols. It covers managed objects for subnetworks that use the IEEE 802.5 Token Ring technology, described in IEEE Standard 802.5-1989. The memo is a replacement for RFC 1231.

It is written for the SNMPv2 Network Management Framework, which has four parts: the SMI (RFC 1442), the core MIB-II objects (STD 17, RFC 1213), the administrative model (RFC 1445) and the protocol for reaching managed objects (RFC 1448).

Objects are defined with a subset of ASN.1. Each object type is named by an OBJECT IDENTIFIER, and the type together with an instance identifies one specific value.
sections.eli5: Imagine a control panel for a toy train loop. This document lists every dial and light on the panel so that every maker builds the same one.

sections.title: Three Tables and Some Identifiers
sections.content:
The memo defines three tables. The 802.5 Interface Table holds state and parameter information specific to 802.5 interfaces. The 802.5 Statistics Table holds interface statistics. The 802.5 Timer Table holds the values of 802.5-defined timers, but it is obsolete and kept only for backward compatibility.

A managed system has one entry in the Interface Table and one in the Statistics Table for each of its 802.5 interfaces. The memo also defines OBJECT IDENTIFIER values that name interface tests (for the ifTestTable) and Token Ring chip sets.

All MAC addresses in the module use the MacAddress textual convention, in the canonical order of IEEE 802.1a (as if sent least significant bit first), even though 802.5 sends MAC addresses most significant bit first. A 16-bit address is shown by setting its upper 4 octets to zero, so AAFF becomes 00000000AAFF.
sections.eli5: There are two panels in use, one showing what the computer is doing and one counting mistakes. A third, old panel is kept only so old tools still work.

sections.title: Fitting In With the Interfaces MIB
sections.content:
When used with the older interfaces group, an 802.5 interface maps one-to-one to an interface in RFC 1213, so the ifIndex value identifies the matching instances of the new objects. RFC 1573 requires every media-specific MIB module to clarify several areas, and this memo does so.

  • Layering: typically no sub-layers sit above or below the 802.5 interface, though the module does not forbid them.
  • Virtual circuits: 802.5 does not support them.
  • ifTestTable: two tests are defined, Insertion and Loopback, and implementing them is not required.
  • ifRcvAddressTable: it lists all unicast, multicast and broadcast MAC addresses the interface accepts, including functional addresses. For functional addresses only one entry is required.
  • ifPhysAddress: it holds the interface MAC address as an octet string of length 6, in IEEE 802.1a canonical order.
  • ifType: the objects apply to each interface whose ifType is iso88025-tokenRing(9).
sections.eli5: This part says how the Token Ring panel plugs into the general panel that every network card has, and answers the questions that general panel left open.

sections.title: The Interface Table
sections.content:
The dot5Table has one entry per 802.5 interface, indexed by dot5IfIndex, which has the same value as ifIndex. Systems with 802.5 interfaces must implement it in addition to the ifTable.

The main objects are:

  • dot5Commands is read-write. Setting it to open(2), reset(3) or close(4) asks the station to enter the ring, reset (keeping MIB counters if possible) or leave the ring. Setting noop(1) does nothing, and reading it always gives noop(1). Open and close correspond to the up and down values of ifAdminStatus.
  • dot5RingStatus is a sum of condition values from 0 to 262143, such as 32 for Ring Recovery, 2048 for Lobe Wire Fault and 4096 for Transmit Beacon. Before an open completes it shows the no-status value 131072.
  • dot5RingState gives the state of entering or leaving the ring (opened, closed, opening, closing, openFailure, ringFailure), and dot5RingOpenStatus gives the result or failure reason of the latest attempt to enter.
  • dot5RingSpeed is the ring speed at the next insertion: unknown, one, four or sixteen megabit. It can differ from the current speed in ifSpeed.
  • dot5UpStream is the MAC address of the upstream neighbor. dot5ActMonParticipate says whether the interface joins the Active Monitor election, and dot5Functional is the bit mask of functional addresses it accepts. dot5LastBeaconSent is the sysUpTime when a Beacon frame was last sent.
sections.eli5: This is the main panel. It has a button to join or leave the ring, a light that says how the ring is doing, and a note saying who the neighbor is.

sections.title: The Statistics Table
sections.content:
The dot5StatsTable has one entry per interface, and systems with 802.5 interfaces must implement it. Every statistic is a Counter32, a 32-bit wrap-around counter. If the hardware keeps 16-bit counters, the agent has to read them often enough to avoid losing significance.

The 18 counters count events defined by 802.5. Examples include line errors (a bad frame check or a non-data bit), burst errors (no transitions for five half-bit timers), abort delimiters sent while transmitting, receive congestion (a frame for this station but no buffer space), soft errors, hard errors, signal loss and transmitted beacons.

Some counters also describe state changes. A lobe wire fault (an open or short circuit in the lobe data path) closes the adapter, and receiving a Remove Ring Station MAC frame makes the interface enter the close state. The singles counter records times the interface sensed that it was alone on the ring, which happens when it is the first one up or when there is a hardware problem.
sections.eli5: This panel is a set of tally counters, one for each kind of hiccup, so a helper can see what has been going wrong and how often.

sections.title: Timers, Tests and Chip Sets
sections.content:
The dot5TimerTable is marked obsolete but is retained for backward compatibility. It would have held read-only timers in units of 100 microseconds, such as the holding time a station may transmit after capturing a token and the no-token recovery timeout.

Two tests are defined as object identities under dot5Tests. The Insert Function test exercises the hardware insert logic, and the text warns that it inserts the station into the network and could cause problems on an operational network. The Full-Duplex Loop Back test checks the path from memory through the chip set and back.

Three chip sets are identified: IBM's 16/4 Mbs chip set, the Texas Instruments TMS 380 4Mbs chip set and the TMS 380C16 16/4 Mbs chip set. They are kept because RFC 1573 obsoletes the older ifExtnsChipSet object that used to identify chip sets.
sections.eli5: This part holds the old stopwatch panel, a couple of self-check buttons, and a list of the brands of parts inside the machine.

sections.title: Compliance Rules
sections.content:
An SNMPv2 entity that claims to implement the module must support two mandatory groups. dot5StateGroup collects the Interface Table objects (commands, ring status, state, open status, speed, upstream address, Active Monitor participation, functional addresses and last beacon time). dot5StatsGroup collects the 18 statistics.

The compliance statement relaxes two objects: write access to dot5ActMonParticipate and to dot5Functional is not required, so they can be read-only.
sections.eli5: The rules say which panels every maker must include, and that a couple of dials may be look-only instead of turnable.

sections.title: Changes From RFC 1231
sections.content:
Appendix A lists what changed from RFC 1231. The module now uses the SNMPv2 SMI. The link between the open and close values of dot5Commands and ifAdminStatus was clarified, as was the relationship between dot5RingSpeed and ifSpeed.

Write access to dot5ActMonParticipate and dot5Functional became optional, and a change to the Active Monitor setting takes effect at the next election. The new object dot5LastBeaconSent was added, the Timer Table was made obsolete, and text on the use of RFC 1573 was added.

On security, the memo says only that security issues are not discussed.
sections.eli5: This is the list of fixes made since the last version: newer wording, a few clearer dials, one new light and one panel retired.
